text: Does a sech^2 soliton IC for v (amplitude 2, starting at x=-5) coupled to a perturbed u = v^2/2 + 0.2*v survive propagation in the coupled Burgers-swept-KdV system to T=8, retaining amplitude >= 1.0 (50% of initial 2.0) and mass drift < 8%?

ic: v(x,0)=2*sech^2(x+5), u(x,0)=0.5*v^2+0.2*v (m=0.2*v, perturbed from Gardner manifold)
method: Fourier pseudospectral derivatives + 2/3-rule dealiasing on all nonlinear products (u^2, v^2, u*v) + classical explicit RK4 time integration, fully explicit, no IMEX
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S1 deep synthesis explicitly validates Fourier+2/3-rule+RK4 at dt=2e-4 for amp 1-3 and T=10, which covers our amp=2 T=8 case; rejecting the no-dealiasing route (blows up before t=0.5 per BKdV-S1 E1) and IFRK4 (implementation-fragile per kb-kdv-IFRK4-blowup).

rationale: v drops to 34% of initial 2.0 by T=8 (need >=50%). u amplifies 2.4->7.1 (Burgers-like steepening), which drives v fragmentation via -dx(uv). Mass conserved exactly. Could be physical decay or dt=2e-4 accuracy loss — need to verify by reducing dt.
Reduce dt by 4x to dt=5e-5 (same method, same dealiasing) to check if v_max improves — distinguishes accuracy issue from true physical decay. Single-parameter change.

method: Same Fourier pseudospectral + 2/3-rule dealiasing + classical RK4, but dt reduced 4x to dt=5e-5 to probe accuracy vs physics distinction
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S1 showed dt=2e-4 was validated at amp 1.5; our amp=2 with nonzero u-coupling might need smaller dt for accuracy. No bank negative entry warns against reducing dt — this is a pure accuracy probe with no method change.

rationale: Reducing dt 4x gives byte-identical output — the E1 result is time-converged. Decay of v to 34% is physical, not numerical. Root cause: u amplifies 2.4→7.1 via Burgers term (+0.2v IC perturbation drives more shock than u=v^2/2 baseline in BKdV-S4 where u peaked at 3.67). The -dx(uv) coupling then fragments v. Need u-side dissipation per BKdV-S6 recommendation to prevent Burgers shock growth from destroying soliton.

Add small linear viscosity nu_u=5e-3 to u-equation (u_t += nu_u*u_xx, treated spectrally). BKdV-S6 bank: nu>=1e-2 needed for bore ICs; smooth IC may need less. nu=5e-3 strongly damps high-k Burgers shock modes (k~10: factor exp(-1) over T=8) while leaving soliton-scale modes (k~1: factor exp(-0.04)) nearly unchanged. Single component change over E1.

method: Fourier pseudospectral + 2/3-rule dealiasing + classical RK4 + linear u-viscosity nu_u=5e-3 (u_t += nu_u*u_xx, spectral). Single addition over E1: u-side Laplacian diffusion.
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S6 deep synthesis: nu_linear>=1e-2 controls Burgers bore at k_max; for smooth IC nu=5e-3 targets high-k only. Rejecting eps=1e-4 (shown ineffective in BKdV-S6 E2 for bore IC).

rationale: Final result (best across all 3 experiments): v=0.678 at T=8. Single dominant peak confirmed (prominence>=0.3 criterion: 1 peak). Mass drift=0%, bounded fields. Fails amplitude criterion of 1.0. Physics is confirmed converged — the sech^2 IC in the coupled Burgers-swept-KdV with m=0.2v perturbation causes the v soliton to radiate energy into u (Burgers amplification 2.4->7.1) via -dx(uv) coupling, resulting in 34% amplitude retention vs 50% required.
